hudson.model.BooleanParameterDefinition.name: submit
hudson.model.BooleanParameterDefinition.description: if set to true the files will be submitted

hudson.tasks.Shell.command: set -e # Prerequisite check, before the 30+ minutes of file generation below. zfin_genes.gff3 is not # produced by this job -- Download-Files_d runs generateGff3.sh, which writes it into # $TARGETROOT/home/data_transfer/Downloads -- and nothing expresses that dependency, so a stale or # never-populated Downloads directory used to surface as a bare "cp: cannot stat" after the whole # generation had already run and left its artifacts in the checkout. GFF3_SOURCE=$TARGETROOT/home/data_transfer/Downloads/zfin_genes.gff3 if [ -f "$GFF3_SOURCE" ]; then echo "Found $GFF3_SOURCE" elif [ -n "$ALLIANCE_RELEASE_VERSION" ]; then # Required: validateAllianceFiles.sh submits/validates it as the GFF file of the release. echo "ERROR: $GFF3_SOURCE is missing, and ALLIANCE_RELEASE_VERSION is set" >&2 echo " ('$ALLIANCE_RELEASE_VERSION'), so this run has to submit a GFF file." >&2 echo " Run Download-Files_d to regenerate it, then re-run this job." >&2 exit 1 else # Not required: with no release version validateAllianceFiles.sh skips the validate/submit # routine entirely, so the file is never read and generation can go ahead without it. echo "NOTE: $GFF3_SOURCE is missing. ALLIANCE_RELEASE_VERSION is empty, so no files are" echo " submitted or validated and the GFF is not needed; continuing without it." echo " Run Download-Files_d first if you intended a real submission." fi

set -e cd $SOURCEROOT/server_apps/DB_maintenance/Alliance && rm -f ZFIN*.json* zfin_genes.gff3 && cp $SOURCEROOT/ZFIN*.json . && gzip ZFIN*.json
# zfin_genes.gff3 comes from Download-Files_d, not from this job (see the prerequisite check in the # first build step). Copy it when it is there; only insist on it when a release version means # validateAllianceFiles.sh is actually going to submit or validate a GFF file. Copying it # unconditionally failed generation-only runs on a file they were never going to read. GFF3_SOURCE=$TARGETROOT/home/data_transfer/Downloads/zfin_genes.gff3 if [ -f "$GFF3_SOURCE" ]; then cp "$GFF3_SOURCE" . elif [ -n "$ALLIANCE_RELEASE_VERSION" ]; then echo "ERROR: $GFF3_SOURCE went missing since the prerequisite check; cannot submit a GFF" >&2 echo " file for release '$ALLIANCE_RELEASE_VERSION'. Run Download-Files_d." >&2 exit 1 else echo "NOTE: $GFF3_SOURCE not present; skipping it (no release version, so it is unused)." fi
cd $SOURCEROOT/server_apps/DB_maintenance/Alliance && ./validateAllianceFiles.sh $submit $ALLIANCE_RELEASE_VERSION

mv $SOURCEROOT/ZFIN*.json $DOWNLOAD_DIRECTORY/current
# createZfinExpressionInfoFile is part of createAllianceFiles, but its output is named in # lower case and so never matched the ZFIN*.json glob above -- it was neither published # nor removed, and accumulated in the checkout. Move it along with its siblings. Left as a # plain mv rather than rm -f: the file is written unconditionally by a task in the # createAllianceFiles graph, so a missing one means generation broke and should fail here. mv $SOURCEROOT/zfin_wt_expression.json $DOWNLOAD_DIRECTORY/current
# validateAllianceFiles.sh reads authorization.txt and every filename relative to its own # directory, so the submission set has to be staged inside the checkout. Clear it out once # the submission has gone through -- the only tracked file in that directory is the script # itself, so everything staged there was left behind after every run. A failed validation # skips this builder and keeps the artifacts for debugging; the rm at the top of the # previous builder clears them on the next run. rm -f $SOURCEROOT/server_apps/DB_maintenance/Alliance/ZFIN*.json.gz rm -f $SOURCEROOT/server_apps/DB_maintenance/Alliance/zfin_genes.gff3
